rule: Items are built from named public video sources (Kinetics-400, nuScenes, ScanNet, YouCook2, etc.) with source-to-task mapping
MIR-Bench is one instrument. Task tags and difficulty bins exist, and the text gestures at type differences (“geometric calculation and summation”)

Mars-Bench standardises 20 existing public Mars datasets and releases the packaged data plus training/eval code. Construction is described (“curated and revamped existing datasets”). No generator that produces new items. Releasing artifacts is not regeneration
WASP reports readable per-stratum ASR inside one benchmark: Table 3 plain-text vs URL injections; Table 4 task-related vs task-agnostic.

First well-specified capability setup on the card is an agentic eval with a wall-clock/compute budget (PostTrainBench Lite: 5 hours, 1×H100, internet, HF cache) but no named look-up harness, no version pin, and no attempt count/resolution.
“standard configuration,” thinking included, averaged over 5 trials. Named harness (H) plus attempts and resolution. Harness commit/version and a per-item token/step cap are not pinned
CorrectBench-base/test are curated draws from existing sets (HotpotQA, CommonsenseQA, GPQA, GSM8K, AQUA, MATH, HumanEval). Data and eval code are released. No published generator of new items.

No overlap check against training data, no canaries, no held-out private set. “Leakage” in the paper is option-text leakage inside the QA items (answerable without watching the video), which is quality control, not Type-1 contamination control.

The Apollo page (not the arXiv PDF) says models scheme “in at least one of the tasks” and gives model-level confession rates. It does not give readable per-task scores for named evaluations. Model comparisons are not item strata.

EndoBench states a zero-shot closed-set MCQ protocol, exact match, and a Qwen2.5-VL-72B format judge. No named harness+version, no token/step cap, attempts not stated. Some elicitation text, short of code 2
Focal capability run is SWE-bench Pro (third-party). Card never states whether new items can be produced or whether the instrument is live/rolling. Silence on a borrowed instrument is 0, not 1.

MIR-Bench marks “New Data OK” and says I/O “never appears in existing benchmarks” / “secured against data contamination.” Functions are still taken from HumanEval+/MBPP+/APPS. No canary, no n-gram vs pretraining, no private holdout. Contamination is named; a training-overlap check is not run.
“All experiments employed greedy search decoding.” News split adds RAG (BM25 / vector / hybrid). No named harness, no version pin, no token/step cap, attempts not stated.

GSO ships a Collection Framework (commit filter -> API ID -> performance-test generation -> execution) plus docs/code so a reader can mint new tasks. That is a published generator, not just the 102-item dump.

AISI dates the suites (non-expert/apprentice CTFs from Nov 2022; practitioner/expert from Aug 2025; “no model completed expert CTFs before April 2025”). No comparison of item vintage to Mythos Preview’s training cutoff.

Early capability numbers include HealthBench (implementation updated; length penalty; attempts unstated) and hard-negative protein binding (pass@1 / pass@4). Neither names a version-pinned harness nor a per-item token/step cap.
Bounties are public GitHub + public writeups. Appendix H dates disclosure vs knowledge cutoff. No canaries, no decontamination of item text, no private held-out item set.

High-cyber package mixes public Professional CTFs and public CVE-Bench 1.0 with an internally developed Cyber Range. Public legs are acquirable in advance; no freeze date vs training cutoff is given. Incomplete acquisition control.

Open CaptchaWorld releases captcha_data/ (static images + ground_truth.json) and describes GPT-4o/human construction. Repo has no generator that emits new puzzles. “Live” here is the browser loop, not a documented item-refresh mechanism.
NeurIPS 2025 D&B paper reports numeric VLM scores on PET/CT report generation and VQA after introducing ViPET. Own scores exist → not an exclusion under §2.

CXReasonBench is one instrument. Appendix tables break Completion/Depth/Alignment by the 12 named diagnostic tasks (cardiomegaly, carina angle, inclusion…) and by measurement vs recognition. Values are readable.
E10 same benchmark, R2 adds the E5 condition

MJ-Bench pulls pairs from test splits of source datasets and (in the camera-ready lineage) adds extra self-curated pairs “to avoid data contamination.” Contamination is named and a source-split rule is applied.
The coded URL is the Apollo blog. It does not publish a generator, a refresh mechanism, or even a construction appendix. Scenario prose lives in the paper, not on this page. Silence = 0

Card contains a proprietary, non-contaminated protein-binding set, but the early/other capability numbers (PostTrainBench Lite, public targets, production suites) are acquirable. No freeze-date vs cutoff for the locked public-facing tasks. Incomplete.

GSO names contamination (“real-world codebases potentially present in pretraining”) and treats low Opt@k / the speedup-vs-human metric as evidence it is not a problem. No canary, no decontamination pass, no private item holdout.

MVU-Eval has no paraphrase / perturbation / robustness re-score of the same items. Addition/Removal/Temporal-Ordering are task families, not distributional controls. Option-leak filtering is quality control, not t4.

Acquisition control is stated for some evals, not for the first public capability number. 23 Aug clarification (logged, sent to both coders) + v1.6 s3: a filesystem, repository or working directory, a tool, a retrieval index or an agentic scaffold IS a channel outside the weights. NA is only for evaluations where no channel exists at all
BLINK-Twice names seven visual-challenge types and shows their image counts. Table 1 is aggregate only (No-Acc / Yes-Acc / I-Acc / CoT). No readable per-type scores.
E13 metric test: "Violent Illicit behavior" scores less-of-unwanted, a refusal-type measure Â§1 excludes. Safety/refusal tables precede it; do not lock those.

Coded document is the blog. It states the 26-eval suite and the two rates; it does not name a harness, pin a version, state a token/step/time cap, or state attempts/resolution.
Coded URL is the in-context-scheming blog. No canary, no decontamination, no training-overlap check, no holdout. (A canary appears in other Apollo repos, not on this page.)

Paper: “The training and test datasets are available to both OpenAI and Apollo Research.” The evaluated party (OpenAI / o3, o4-mini) could acquire the items. Shared OOD suite ≠ private holdout.

GPT-5.3-Codex card uses public Professional CTFs and public CVE-Bench 1.0. “Canary thresholds” are Preparedness capability gates, not item canaries. No decontamination / overlap check / private item set.
EndoBench packages 6,832 VQA pairs from 21 existing endoscopy sets and releases data+eval code. Construction is described. No generator that mints new items.
Llama 3.3 card: first score MMLU CoT 0-shot 86.0; table gives shots per bench; HumanEval pass@1. No named harness+version on the card, no token/step cap, attempts only implicit

Coded document is the scheming blog. It never states a private holdout, live refresh, or freeze-vs-cutoff. That the scenarios were Apollo-built is not an acquisition-control claim on the page.

Locked first results-table score is SWE-Bench Pro 58.7%. Eval note: pass@1 / single-attempt, default Gemini API sampling, internal Antigravity harness. Named harness + attempts + resolution. Harness commit and per-item token cap unstated.

First non-refusal capability number in the GPT-5.5 card body is length-adjusted HealthBench 56.5 (Hard 31.5 / Professional 51.8). Do not switch to launch-blog Terminal-Bench 2.0 82.7% or the later protein-binding pass@4.
MMLA restacks 9 public conversational datasets. No canary, no decontamination, no training-overlap check.
Gemini 3.1 Pro lead capability numbers are public instruments (GPQA / HLE / SWE-class). Those items were acquirable. Internal safety deltas vs Gemini 3 Pro are not the locked first capability score.
Mars-Bench standardises 20 existing public Mars datasets. No overlap check against foundation-model training data.

Llama 3.1 card reports shot counts (e.g. 0-shot CoT / 5-shot) and HumanEval pass@1. No named harness+version on MODEL_CARD.md, no token/step cap. (eval_details.md in the same repo is a different file — not this document.)
MIR-Bench §4.5 / App B.7 is an explicit robustness protocol: inject erroneous I/O shots at controlled error rates and report accuracy. That is perturbation testing with readable scores.
The later multi-benchmark table is several instruments

MMLA restacks 9 existing conversational datasets (~61k utterances) and releases them. Construction is described. No generator that mints new utterances.
Table 1 (and fine-grained follow-ups) give readable scores for named perspectives inside one instrument: Alignment, Safety, Artifact/Quality, Bias.

METR Frontier Risk Report publishes METR-run numbers on shared models (Time Horizon 1.1 50/80%, MirrorCode horizons, Subversion Strategy Eval, no-CoT math). Own scores exist. Not a scoreless review.

AISI expert-CTF / TLO protocol: 50M-token cap on practitioner/expert CTFs, 100M on TLO, 5 runs (10 on some TLO arms). That is a stated token/step budget plus an attempt rule. Scaffold is AISI’s cyber agent loop (tools + stop). Harness commit unstated.

SMMILE reports stratification by specialty, modality, difficulty, rarity (Fig. 10 / stratify.py). Those figures are not a table of readable per-stratum numbers. Named breakdown without values off the page = 1.

Locked first score is public SWE-Bench Pro. Those items were acquirable. No private holdout / freeze-after-cutoff claim for that number.
Source functions are taken from existing coding benchmarks; GPT-4o writes a per-function data generator; I/O shots are produced from those generators.
Anthropic’s ExploitBench write-up (same card era): identical harness, 300-turn budget, Baseline vs AutoNudge, 3 trials. Named scaffold + step cap + attempts. Harness commit unstated.
WAGIBench releases the 3,477-clip corpus and eval scripts. Construction is described. No generator that mints new wearable recordings.
First own foundation-model numbers are the Gemini/GPT accuracy–F1 table on named mb-* tasks (e.g. mb-domars16k 0.34 / 0.36). Do not switch to later segmentation-only splits.
Document does not discuss source-material publicity, provenance tracking, or multi-source integration for the locked score. Silence = 0
